content.comment_body: Hello, I am working on programming a [article_no] to show the RPM value of a motor. My goal is to 'sample and hold' the incoming frequency, apply a calculation to convert it to RPM, and then display this result on the [product_name]'s display with a refresh rate of one second. Can anyone offer guidance? Thank you, [user_name].

You can use the high-speed counter (HSC) function. Here is a link: [url]. This question has been discussed for a [version_no]; try to understand the concept and then apply it to [product_name]. Hope this helps. Best regards.

Yes, this is straightforward. First, count the pulses at the input using a counter. Perform this each second. Using the value from the counter, calculate (for example, multiply by 60) and then reset the counter. This will give you revolutions (impulses) per minute.

Thank you for your reply—I've successfully configured the [product_name] to display the RPM value. Is it possible to also show this value on an external HMI panel? If so, could you explain how to achieve this? I am new to [product_name] and [product_name], and for my university project, I plan to control a drive through both HMI and [product_name].

Yes, that is also possible. First, you need to perform variable mapping for the value you wish to display on the panel. Go to Tools > Parameter Variable Mapping and configure the settings appropriately. In this program, I have already done the same setup for you. In [product_name], you can program this value (in the variable list) and set it on your panel.

analysis.insight_summary: Users explored methods for displaying motor RPM on a [product_name], moving from frequency measurement to calculation and visualization on the module itself, as well as on an external HMI. The main user experience insight reveals a desire for simple, integrated data flow and display across different hardware. Some uncertainty was expressed around connecting and configuring variable mapping in external panels for real-time display.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward way to set up [product_name] for accurate RPM display and to interface effortlessly with an external HMI panel for enhanced control and visualization.
